diagnostic_evidence.quote: with output $\|{\rm T}(\theta;\cdot)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^D)}\leq R$ and weight magnitude $\|\theta\|_{\infty}\leq \kappa$
In addition, we assume $\|f\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathcal{M}(q))}\le R$ for some $R>0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership in $\mathcal{T}(\ldots,R,\kappa)$ requires $\|{\rm T}\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^D)}\le R$ on all of $\mathbb{R}^D$. The proof of thmApprox (via Props repetatildei/approxetai) controls the network only on $[0,1]^D$ or $\mathcal{M}(q)$; no step establishes global boundedness, and the construction violates it: the guarded arithmetic (ReLU guards such as $\sigma(cs+M)-M$) is exact only for bounded inputs, and off the guard region the computed $\|\tilde\eta(x)\|_1$ can reach $K(1+2M)$, so the power-series approximation of $1/\|\tilde\eta(x)\|_1$ produces outputs growing with powers of $K$; the output is unbounded on $\mathbb{R}^D$. The same unestablished $R$-bound appears in the class-membership claims of Props repetatildei and approxetai, and the bias step of thmGeneralization needs an $\epsilon$-approximant inside the ERM class whose $R$-bound also enters the variance estimate.

failure_location.quote: there exists a transformer network ${\rm T}(\theta;\cdot)\in\mathcal{T}(L_{\rm T}, m_{\rm T},d_{embed},\ell,L_{\rm FFN},w_{\rm FFN},R,\kappa)$ with parameters

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Append a final clipping FFN block adding the tokenwise correction $-\sigma(s-R)+\sigma(-R-s)$ to the readout entry (clipping cannot increase the on-tube error since $|f|\le R$ by Assumption assumpf), and clip the propositions' outputs to $[0,1]$; all stated parameters, rates and scopes survive up to absorbed constants.
issues.overall_effect: The output-boundedness part of class membership in thmApprox and in Props repetatildei/approxetai is unproven and false for the given constructions; the bias step of thmGeneralization lacks a valid in-class approximator as written.
issues.title: Global output bound required for class membership is never established and is violated by the constructed networks
issues.why_classification: A short, local, standard construction (output clipping) repairs the missing boundedness while preserving every stated guarantee, rate and advertised scope; only the routine check that clipping is harmless is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $M>0$, and $c=(c^1,\cdots,c^D)$ and $x=(x^1,\cdots,x^D)$ be vectors in $\mathbb{R}^D$ be such that $\|c\odot x\|_{\infty}\leq M$

issues.failure_explanation: No kappa bound in the paper is derived (each is asserted by 'reexamining the proof'), and the assertions contradict each other: the proof of Prop approxetai claims the network $T_1$ implementing all $\tilde\eta_i$'s and their sum has $\kappa=O(D^2\delta^{-2d})$ (only $d,q,\tau,\mathrm{Vol}$ hidden), while Prop repetatildei claims each single $\tilde\eta_i$ already requires $\kappa=O(D^2\delta^{-8})$; for $d\le 3$ this is impossible since $T_1$ contains each component's weights and delta-powers cannot be hidden. Moreover, the guards forced by the construction (multiplying $\|P(z_i)^\top(x-z_i)\|^2\le dD$ on $[0,1]^D$ by $(h\delta)^{-2}$) have magnitude $\Theta(dD\delta^{-2})$, and inserting these with $\ell=\Theta(Dd)$ into the Interaction Lemma's bound $O(d_{embed}^4\mu^2\ell^2M^2)$ yields scaling like $D^6d^6\delta^{-8}$ rather than the claimed $D^2$. Hence the explicit kappa guarantees of thmApprox, thmGeneralization and the propositions are unsupported and, in their explicit $D$-dependence, not obtainable from the paper's own tools.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the weight accounting with explicit guard constants (of order $dD\delta^{-2}$) and token counts, resolve the $\delta^{-2d}$ vs $\delta^{-8}$ inconsistency, and restate the kappa bounds in Props repetatildei/approxetai and Theorems thmApprox/thmGeneralization accordingly (possibly with higher $D$-powers); all rates and other guarantees are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The stated weight-magnitude guarantees in thmApprox and thmGeneralization (and both propositions) are unreliable; if the true required kappa exceeds the class parameter in thmGeneralization, the epsilon-approximator is not in the ERM class and the bias step fails. The final generalization rate survives because kappa enters the covering number only logarithmically.
issues.title: Weight-magnitude (kappa) bounds are underived and mutually inconsistent (delta^{-2d} vs delta^{-8} for the same construction)
issues.why_classification: The quantitative kappa guarantee of the main theorems is not established, is internally contradicted, and may have to be weakened (limited quantitative loss); repairing it requires a contained but nontrivial recomputation of the weight bookkeeping, though no proof architecture change or rate loss is involved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: ${\rm B}(H) = {\rm FFN}({\rm MHA}(H) + H) + {\rm MHA}(H) + H.
For the feed-forward layer of $B_8$, we take the weight matrix equals to identity and bias equals to zero, so that it implements the identity operation.

issues.failure_explanation: In the block $B(H)=FFN(MHA(H)+H)+MHA(H)+H$ the FFN output is added to the post-attention matrix, so preserving a token requires the FFN to output 0 there, and subtracting a constant requires outputting the negative constant. The Gating Lemma as stated outputs values ($h_t$ on kept tokens, zeroed data rows otherwise), which in this block would double the kept tokens and the positional rows; it also performs no constant subtraction. Likewise the 'identity' FFN in the proof of Prop repetatildei would double every entry instead of preserving. Hence the final FFN step of every arithmetic-operation proof fails to establish the claimed block output, and the required correction-FFNs (position-dependent constant subtraction/zeroing) are never constructed or cited.

failure_location.quote: Then we apply the Gating Lemma \ref{Gatinglemma} to have a $\mathcal{FFN}(3)$ to subtract off the constant $DM$ in the $D+1$-th column.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and prove a corrected gating lemma producing the needed correction-FFN (e.g. $FFN(h_t)=-c\,\mathbb{1}[\text{position in a range}]e_1$ with zero output on preserved tokens, implementable by thresholds on $\mathcal{I}_t$ with weights $O(\ell M)$), or consistently amend the block definition, and adjust the arithmetic-lemma proofs; all stated results and bounds then survive.
issues.overall_effect: All exact-representation lemmas for arithmetic operations, both propositions, and both main theorems have invalid final assembly steps as written; every downstream claim rests on them.
issues.title: Gating/FFN steps of the arithmetic-lemma proofs are incompatible with the residual transformer block (would double preserved tokens; no constant subtraction)
issues.why_classification: A genuinely missing lemma/construction (the correction-FFN) plus edits to every arithmetic proof are required, but a contained repair exists that preserves all statements, rates and scopes; hence neither minor nor serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: ${\rm DE}:\mathbb{R}^{d_{embed}\times\ell}\to\mathbb{R}$ is the decoding layer which outputs the first element in the last column.

there exists ${\rm T}(\theta;\cdot)=({\rm T}^1(\theta;\cdot),\cdots,{\rm T}^K(\theta;\cdot))$ with each ${\rm T}^i(\theta;\cdot)\in\mathcal{T}(L_T, m_T,d_{embed},\ell,L_{\rm FFN},w_{\rm FFN},R,\kappa)$

issues.failure_explanation: The class $\mathcal{T}$ has a fixed decoder returning the first entry of the last column. The constructions place their results in interior columns followed by zero padding (e.g. $\tilde\eta_i(x)$ at column $(d+3)D+2d+7$, with padding up to column $\ell$), so the literally constructed network outputs 0, not the claimed value; no step routes the result into the last column. Moreover, Prop approxetai claims a $K$-vector of networks each belonging to the scalar-output class $\mathcal{T}$, which the single fixed decoder cannot produce (each component would need to read a different column).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Route each final computed value into the last column (feasible by the placement flexibility of Remark rmkflexibility at no parameter cost), and for approxetai let the decoder read a specified column per component or restate the components accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The output claims of Props repetatildei and approxetai, and the final network identity in the proof of thmApprox (hence thmGeneralization's approximator), are not established as written.
issues.title: Constructed networks never route results to the decoder's readout (last column); vector-valued claim conflicts with the fixed scalar decoder
issues.why_classification: A short, local, routine rerouting/decoder-convention fix preserves all claims and parameter bounds; only the final readout step is missing.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we make the assumption that the logarithmic term $\ln(\frac{1}{\epsilon})$ is much smaller than the exponential term $\delta^{-d}$. Although it is not always the case

issues.failure_explanation: The tolerance $\epsilon$ and net scale $\delta$ in Prop approxetai are independent, and the proof's own derivation gives $m_T=O(\max(D\delta^{-d},\ln(1/\epsilon)+K))$ and $\ell\ge O(D\delta^{-d}+\ln(1/\epsilon)+K)$. Asserting $O(D\delta^{-d})$ requires $\ln(1/\epsilon)\lesssim\delta^{-d}$, an assumption acknowledged only in Remark log ('Although it is not always the case') and absent from the proposition's hypotheses; e.g. for fixed $\delta$ and $\epsilon=e^{-\delta^{-2d}}$ the stated bounds are false. Theorems thmApprox/thmGeneralization are unaffected because they set the tolerance to $\delta^\alpha$, where the regime holds.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $\ln(1/\epsilon)\le C\delta^{-d}$ to the statement (as in Remark log), or restate $m_T=O(D\delta^{-d}+\ln(1/\epsilon))$ and $\ell\ge O(D\delta^{-d}+\ln(1/\epsilon))$.
issues.overall_effect: Prop approxetai, advertised as a reusable building block, overclaims its head and token counts outside the regime $\ln(1/\epsilon)\lesssim\delta^{-d}$; no downstream theorem is affected.
issues.title: Proposition approxetai's stated m_T and ell bounds drop the ln(1/epsilon) term and hold only under an unstated regime
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis addition or restatement repairs it; all downstream results, which operate in the valid regime, are unchanged.
